Re: Internal Appeal of Prior Authorization Denial  
Member: Sawyer Carter  
Member ID: W602896534  
Reference number: POC-29630AA1D9-59024  
Requested service: Total ankle replacement  
CPT: 27702  
Date of denial notice: August 4, 2026

To the Appeals Department:

I appeal the denial of prior authorization for total ankle replacement, CPT 27702. The denial states that the submitted records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment. The records do document extensive conservative treatment, including supervised physical therapy, medication, and injection treatment, without adequate or durable relief.

The patient has had 24 months of progressive ankle pain that is not relieved by rest. Conservative treatment has included:

- Twelve weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on ankle strengthening and balance, from April 8, 2026, through July 1, 2026, with 18 visits completed. This treatment is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- NSAID treatment for six months, with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on April 13, 2026, which provided only four weeks of partial relief.

The patient continues to have clinically significant impairment despite this treatment. The patient ambulates with an antalgic gait and is limited to approximately two blocks. Examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. Weight-bearing ankle radiographs dated June 20, 2026, show tibiotalar joint-space obliteration with subchondral cysts, demonstrating advanced structural ankle disease.

The publicly available BCBSMS policy titled Total Ankle Replacement, policy number L.7.01.428, states:

“Total ankle replacement using an FDA-approved device may be considered medically necessary in skeletally mature patients with moderate to severe ankle (tibiotalar) pain that limits daily activity and who have the following conditions:”

The patient’s records support moderate to severe tibiotalar pain that limits daily activity. The 24-month duration, persistent pain despite rest and treatment, antalgic gait, two-block walking limitation, painful restricted motion, and radiographic joint-space obliteration with subchondral cysts support the severity and functional impact of the condition.

The policy also states:

“Total ankle replacement is considered investigational for all other indications.”

This appeal is based on the documented clinical findings and treatment history for this patient’s severe symptomatic tibiotalar disease. The patient has no active infection, is a nonsmoker, has a BMI of 29, and has no untreated substance use. These records do not identify the contraindications listed in the publicly available policy.

The policy text publicly available to me does not state that a particular duration or type of conservative treatment is required before total ankle replacement. Because the denial relies specifically on an alleged inadequate conservative-treatment trial, please identify the exact clinical-review criterion used, provide the complete criterion and the source applicable to this member’s plan, and explain how the attached records fail to satisfy it. If a separate nonpublic clinical-review guideline was applied, please provide that guideline with the appeal determination.

Please reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for total ankle replacement, CPT 27702. In the alternative, please arrange a clinical peer-to-peer review with Reyes, MD, the treating orthopedic surgeon, and provide the complete appeal rationale and the criteria applied.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and advise me if any additional information is required.

Sincerely,

Sawyer Carter  
[Mailing address]  
[Telephone number]  
[Email address]

Attachments:

4. Weight-bearing ankle radiographs and report dated June 20, 2026

6. Copy of the August 4, 2026, denial notice
